subject: English
description: Positive, comparative, superlative; irregular forms; common transformation traps

options.option_text: gooder
better
more good
best

questions.explanation: IRREGULAR comparison: good — better — best. Not 'gooder' (incorrect) or 'more good'. Other irregulars: bad — worse — worst; little — less — least; many/much — more — most; far — farther/further — farthest/furthest. Distractor 4 = superlative.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct transformation: 'No other student in the class is as bright as Rohan' is equivalent to:

options.option_text: Rohan is bright among all students
Rohan is the brightest student in the class
Rohan is brighter than some students in class
Rohan is one of the brightest students in class

questions.explanation: 'No other X is as Y as Z' = 'Z is the Y-est X'. Positive degree negative comparison → SUPERLATIVE. 'Rohan is the brightest student'. Distractor 1 = positive (loses superlative force). Distractor 3 = comparative but weaker. Distractor 4 = 'one of the brightest' implies plural, weaker than 'no other equal'.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correctly comparative form: 'Iron is _____ than aluminium.'

options.option_text: more heavier than aluminium per kilogram
heavier than aluminium of equal volume
much more heavier than aluminium per piece
heaviest among aluminium and the lighter metals

questions.explanation: Comparative of 'heavy' = HEAVIER (one-syllable + -y becomes -ier). Distractor 1 = double-comparative ('more heavier'), grammatically incorrect. Distractor 3 = same fault, even more compounded. Distractor 4 = superlative, doesn't fit 'than'.
questions.subject: English

options.option_text: He is one of the most intelligent boy in his class
He is one of the most intelligent boys in his class
He is the most intelligentest boy in his class
He is more intelligent than any boys in his class

questions.explanation: 'One of the [superlative] X' — X is PLURAL because we are picking from a group. 'One of the most intelligent BOYS'. Distractor 1 wrongly singularises 'boy'. Distractor 3 = double-superlative ('mostest'), wrong. Distractor 4 = 'any boys' incorrect; should be 'any other boy in his class'.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Convert to comparative: 'Mumbai is the most populous city in Maharashtra.'

options.option_text: Mumbai is more populous than every Maharashtra city
Mumbai is more populous than any other city in Maharashtra
Mumbai is more populous than no other city in Maharashtra
Mumbai is one of the most populous cities in Maharashtra

questions.explanation: Superlative → comparative: 'X is the most Y of Z' = 'X is more Y than ANY OTHER Z'. Note 'OTHER' is essential — without it, the sentence becomes 'X is more Y than ANY Z' which would include X itself (logically impossible). Distractor 1 wrongly says 'every', includes Mumbai itself. Distractor 3 has a double-negative. Distractor 4 weakens the original superlative claim.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct comparative form: 'This book is _____ than that one.'

options.option_text: more interesting then that one
more interesting than that one
interestinger than that one
most interesting than that one

questions.explanation: Multi-syllable adjectives form comparative with 'MORE' + adjective: 'more interesting'. Connector is 'THAN' (comparison), not 'then' (temporal sequence). Distractor 1 misuses 'then'. Distractor 3 wrong inflection — multi-syllable adjectives don't take -er. Distractor 4 = superlative form (most), doesn't fit 'than'.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: The superlative of 'far' (when referring to distance) is:

options.option_text: farer or most far in usage
farthest, used for physical distance
more far in nearly all situations
fartest in most British English usage

questions.explanation: FAR — irregular: far / farther / farthest (physical distance) OR far / further / furthest (figurative — 'further details', 'further notice'). Distractor 1 'farer' is wrong. Distractor 3 'more far' is wrong. Distractor 4 'fartest' is incorrect spelling.
